transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

I’m here because people keep saying I’m making something out of nothing. But I know what’s been going on.

My wife’s relative… he came into the house to get at me. My tools don’t just move on their own. And my fishing plans don’t get ruined every weekend by accident. It’s been months of this. Seems pretty clear he’s trying to take over my place and push me out.
Have you been hearing voices, or seeing or sensing things that other people don't seem to notice?
No… I don’t think so. I’m not hearing voices or seeing things like that. It’s not that kind of thing.
Do you have any medical illnesses, or have you been using alcohol, drugs, or any new medications around the time these beliefs started?
I don’t know. I mean… nothing comes to mind. I’m not looking to get into all that—just, I haven’t noticed anything like that around when this started.
Aside from this situation with your wife's relative, how have things been going for you at work and in your day-to-day routine lately?

Mostly normal. I still get up, go to the plant, do my assembly work, pay the bills… take care of myself.

It’s not like I can’t function. The problem is at home. With him, and my things.
Can you tell me exactly how many months this has been going on—when did you first start noticing these things happening?
About nine months, I guess. It started after my wife’s relative moved into our place.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that his wife's relative is sabotaging his belongings and trying to force him out of his home) persisting for approximately 9 months. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, and no other psychotic symptoms reported. Mood symptoms are absent, and functioning is preserved outside the delusional theme (continues working, paying bills, self-care). No evidence of substance use or medical illness that could account for the delusion. This presentation is most consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22), as the criteria for Schizophrenia (F20.0) are not met due to lack of additional psychotic symptoms and preserved functioning, and the delusion is well-systematized and singular in theme rather than the broader presentation seen in F28 (Other psychotic disorder).
